description: GeoLatido was born in Hidalgo del Parral, Chihuahua, out of curiosity to understand how our planet beats. We are a group that combines programming, data analysis, and research to work with NASA's SAR radar images, a technology that can observe the Earth's surface day and night, and through clouds. Our goal is to translate these signals into clear, useful, and accessible software tools for anyone.
summary:
GeoLatido turns NASA–ISRO NISAR radar data into verdicts anyone can read. For each pair of dates over an area, it says one of three things: probable change, no detectable change, or not observable, and in that last case it says why. You can search any city in the world. The app finds the NISAR passes that have HH and HV and reads only that area over HTTPS, in memory, without storing the raw data. It then compares the change in the radar signal with that pair’s own noise. A 0.3° area takes about 2–3 minutes. Each verdict comes with a “receipt” (the data files, thresholds and noise behind it), possible explanations in plain language, and what it does not prove. The app also shows Sentinel-2 photos from before and after, and ground sinking measured from NISAR interferograms (GUNW).

Benefits and intended impact
Radar is hard to read. GeoLatido gives honest answers to people who are not experts, in Spanish and English, with no account needed. Every figure can be traced back to its data. Anyone can ask “could the satellite have seen that event?” For example, the 1 July 2026 flash flood in our home town, Hidalgo del Parral, was not observable: no satellite passed while the water was on the streets. With real data, 2 of 16 pairs in Parral showed probable change. In eastern Mexico City, the ground sinks up to about 186 mm per year. We want civil protection offices, students and local communities to be able to use satellite data without being misled by it.
details:
Data: NISAR GCOV and GUNW, OPERA DSWx-S1, Sentinel-2, Copernicus DEM, plus event catalogues from USGS, GDACS and NASA EONET.

Backend: Python, FastAPI, h5py, rasterio, NumPy and SciPy.

Maps: TiTiler, Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFFs and nginx.

Frontend: React, TypeScript, Vite and MapLibre GL with a 3D globe.

Platform: independent services that run together with Docker Compose.

Hardware: our own 16 GB laptops, with no servers and no GPU.

Process: we wrote the specifications before the code, and used AI coding help (Claude Code). The team checked every figure. The license is Apache-2.0.

Creativity and what we considered

Saying what we don’t know is the core of the product. The three states are shown by shape (filled, outline, hatched), not by colour alone. Thresholds that are not calibrated are labelled as such. The app never claims a cause. Raw radar is never stored on disk. The app explains what SAR measures in plain language.
